body.text: Police have charged a Melbourne man who allegedly played a significant role in spreading online propaganda for the Islamic State terror group.
Mohamed Bakit was arrested during a raid in Carlton this morning after authorities covertly monitored his activities for years.
Mr Bakit has been charged with being a member of a terrorist organisation and is accused of sharing thousands of extremist media files and IS propaganda.
Counterterrorism police have charged a Melbourne man accused of spreading extremist material as an online propagandist for the Islamic State (IS) terror group.
Mohamed Bakit was arrested during a raid on a home in Carlton this morning after authorities covertly monitored his activities for several years.

Addressing media on Wednesday, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said an investigation was launched after Australian Border Force officers found suspicious material on the man's mobile phone following an examination of his luggage at Melbourne Airport before a trip to Egypt in November 2020.
A further search warrant was executed in 2024, with additional electronic devices seized.
Police allege a forensicanalysis of Mr Bakit's devices revealed he pledged allegiance to the terrorist group and acted as an online propagandist.
It is alleged he sent about 10,000 files of violent extremist material and IS propaganda between November 2015 and July 2020.

Among the material were "abhorrent" depictions of executions and torture, material intended to radicalise, and information about carrying out mass casualty attacks, AFP Acting Assistant Commissioner Paula Hudson said.
The assistant commissioner said the scale of the material placed the man as a "principal distributor of ISIS propaganda within the group".
"Terrorist propaganda is not harmless online content," she said.
"Terrorist organisations like ISIS rely on online platforms to distribute propaganda and recruit supporters."
Man accused of terrorist offences denies charges

Mr Bakit, an Australian citizen who lived with his wife, was charged with one count of membership of a terrorist organisation, three counts of using a carriage service to menace, harass or cause offence and one count of possessing or controlling violent extremist material.
The maximum penalty for these offences can include 10 years' imprisonment.
Mr Bakit faced court briefly this afternoon, where his lawyer Stephanie McLennan said he would be applying for bail tomorrow.
Details of the charges and allegations were not read out.
Outside court, Ms McLennan said: "He denies the charges".
At the start of the filing hearing, Mr Bakit was brought into the courtroom wearing a black jumper, maroon shirt and spectacles.
Ms McLennan said it was her client's first time in custody, and that he had previously suffered a stroke, was diabetic and was on blood pressure and cholesterol medication.
"My client is in poor health and has every intention to apply for bail," she said.
Further devices were seized during the Joint Counter Terrorism Team raid of the Carlton home this morning.
However, the AFP said the man was not linked to any particular attacks, and there was no threat to the community.
Assistant Commissioner Hudson did not rule out further arrests as police worked with international partners to disrupt the man's associates.
"We certainly won't be ruling out further arrests in relation to that," she said.
